== Biography ==

The Hatter is a Wonderland resident, described by the Cheshire Cat as quite mad. He hosts a tea party at which he engages in elaborate logical disputation, particularly regarding language and meaning. When his guest claims that "I mean what I say" is the same thing, the Hatter vigorously objects. He argues that such logic would make "I see what I eat" the same as "I eat what I see," employing this paradox to demonstrate the faulty reasoning in his interlocutor's claim. He shows a certain contempt for those unable to follow his arguments, though his own memory is frustratingly unreliable; when questioned, he admits readily to facts he cannot recall.

At the trial of the Knave of Hearts, the Hatter's manner changes entirely. Confronted by the Queen and King, he becomes seized with fear, trembling so violently that he shakes off his very shoes when the Queen stares at him, and dropping his teacup in panic when threatened with execution. He describes himself as a poor man, and his anxious deference to authority stands in sharp contrast to the argumentative confidence he displays at his tea table.

== Relationships ==

'''[[March Hare]]''' — strained friendship. The two appear to maintain both companionship and tension, engaging in debates over logic and meaning at their shared tea table.

'''[[Queen]]''' — adversary. The Queen's anger was once incited against the Hatter, whom she accused of murdering the time and against whom she demanded execution.

'''[[Alice]]''' — acquaintance. The Hatter encounters Alice at the tea party, observing her with curiosity and drawing her into his games of logical disputation.

'''[[Dormouse]]''' — fellow participant. The Dormouse sits asleep between the Hatter and the March Hare at their table, serving as an unwitting cushion for their elbows.

'''[[King]]''' — stern authority. The King summoned the Hatter to give evidence during the trial of the Knave of Hearts and threatened him with execution for his inability to recall what was demanded of him.
